claims.text: What the image looks like Bilateral diffuse interstitial / ground-glass → atypical pneumonia (Mycoplasma); PCP in HIV
claims.quote: Bilateral diffuse interstitial / ground-glass Atypical pneumonia (Mycoplasma); PCP in HIV

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Interstitial pneumonia: increased interstitial markings and subpleural reticular opacities that increase from apex to bases — suggests a viral or mycoplasmal cause
claims.quote: Interstitial pneumonia (on chest radiography, appearing as increased interstitial markings and subpleural reticular opacities that increase from the apex to the bases of the lungs) suggests viral or mycoplasmal etiology.

claims.text: PCP on CXR: characteristically diffuse, bilateral perihilar infiltrates, but 20 to 30% of patients have a normal CXR
claims.quote: Chest radiographs characteristically show diffuse, bilateral perihilar infiltrates, but 20 to 30% of patients have normal radiographs.

claims.text: PCP on CT: often ground-glass infiltrates, even when the CXR is normal; a normal CT has a high negative predictive value and is often used to exclude PCP
claims.quote: A CT scan often shows ground glass infiltrates, even when the chest radiograph is normal. A normal CT scan has a high negative predictive value; therefore, it is often used to exclude a diagnosis of Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia.

claims.text: Buzzword: ground-glass on chest CT = PCP, viral pneumonia, alveolar proteinosis
claims.quote: Ground-glass Chest CT PCP, viral pneumonia, alveolar proteinosis

claims.text: Causes Mycoplasma pneumoniae: a common cause of respiratory infection (URI, acute bronchitis) that causes pneumonia in a subset of patients, particularly community-acquired pneumonia
claims.quote: M. pneumoniae is a common cause of respiratory infections, including acute upper respiratory infection (URI) and acute bronchitis. It can cause pneumonia in a subset of patients, particularly community-acquired pneumonia.

claims.text: Sometimes described as “atypical” because it does not respond to beta-lactam antibiotics as most community-acquired pneumonia does; outbreaks have occurred in congregate settings (schools, summer camps, military facilities)
claims.quote: Because mycoplasma infections do not respond to beta-lactam antibiotics as do most cases of community-acquired pneumonia, they are sometimes described as atypical pathogens. Outbreaks of mycoplasma pneumonia have occurred in congregate settings, including schools, children's summer camps, and military facilities.

claims.text: Pneumocystis jirovecii: an atypical fungus; a common cause of pneumonia in immunosuppressed patients, especially with HIV or on systemic glucocorticoids
claims.quote: Pneumocystis jirovecii, an atypical fungus, is a common cause of pneumonia in immunosuppressed patients, especially in those infected with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and in those receiving systemic glucocorticoids.

claims.text: PCP risk remains high in people unaware of their HIV or not on antiretroviral therapy, especially with CD4 < 200/microL or < 14% (stage 3 HIV)
claims.quote: patients who are not aware that they have HIV or not taking antiretroviral therapy remain at high risk for developing P. jirovecii pneumonia (PCP), especially those with CD4+ T cell counts < 200/microL or < 14% (ie, stage 3 HIV infection) (2).

claims.text: Symptoms PCP: fever, dyspnea and dry cough
claims.quote: Symptoms include fever, dyspnea, and dry cough.

claims.text: PCP exam: fever, tachypnea and tachycardia may be present, particularly on exertion; diffuse crackles may be heard
claims.quote: On examination, fever, tachypnea and tachycardia may be present. Tachypnea and tachycardia may be particularly apparent on exertion. On auscultation, diffuse pulmonary crackles (rales) may be heard over the lung fields.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: macrolide for Mycoplasma; TMP-SMX + steroids for PCP
claims.quote: Macrolide for Mycoplasma; TMP-SMX + steroids for PCP

claims.text: PCP (Merck): sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim (alternatives if sulfa-allergic); add a glucocorticoid if PaO2 < 70 mm Hg or A-a gradient ≥ 35 mm Hg
claims.quote: Treat patients with sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim or use alternate therapies in patients allergic to sulfonamides, adding a glucocorticoid if PaO2 is < 70 mm Hg or A-a gradient is ≥ 35 mm Hg.

claims.text: If HIV is confirmed, start ART, ideally within 2 weeks of the PCP diagnosis
claims.quote: If HIV infection is confirmed, ART must be initiated, ideally within 2 weeks of diagnosis of P. jirovecii pneumonia.
